subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - GPU/throughput discussion
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmeai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - post-call recap

Jordan — great to connect this morning. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we have alignment.

Summary of ask:
- Customer: AcmeAI wants dedicated capacity to support LLM-powered question-answering in their knowledge base product.
- Target throughput: ~200 concurrent requests, 40 tokens per request avg, peak 300 concurrent.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for 8k-context Llama-2-like model.
- Expected monthly token volume: 1.2B – 1.8B tokens (user-generated tokens + system prompts)

Pricing / budget guidance we discussed:
- Target unit economics: customer is aiming for ~$900–1,200 / 1M tokens (all-in cost to them) for dedicated deployment given SLAs.
- They asked for a Reserved/Committed option with predictable monthly price.

Options we proposed (high level):
1) 4x A100 80GB (reserved pool) — handles baseline throughput; strong perf for 8k sequences. Estimated throughput: ~900 tokens/sec total; cost estimate: TBD.
2) 8x A100 80GB (reserved) — recommended for headroom to cover peak concurrency (300 reqs) and tails; supports batching without impacting p95.
3) Alternative: 8x H100 (if available in customer's region) — better token/sec and lower unit cost at scale; higher upfront reservation.

Action items / next steps:
- Jordan: confirm avg tokens per request and monthly active users to refine token/month estimate (by EOD 6/16).
- Marissa/Ben: provide a detailed cost model (per 1M tokens) and a reserved capacity quote with 3 sizing options + optional burst pool (by 6/17).
- Jordan: loop in procurement for contract/PO timing and any legal terms.

I've attached a starter pricing calc that maps tokens -> GPU-hours -> cost and a draft SOW for initial scope. We'll iterate once we get the confirmed token volumes.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0142

Attachments: Dedicated_pricing_calc.xlsx, AcmeAI_Redwood_SOW_draft.pdf

From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmeai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Li <rachel.li@acmeai.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - post-call recap

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap.

Couple clarifications:
- Avg tokens per request looks closer to 30 (not 40) for most flows; however we have a subset (admin queries) that are 120 tokens avg — those are ~10% of traffic.
- Monthly active users: approx 45k MAU, with ~0.8 interactions per user/day on average.
- So ballpark tokens/month: (45k * 0.8 * 30 * 30 days) + admin tail ~= 32M + 12M = ~44M tokens/month — wait that seems low vs your earlier 1.2B.

I think there's confusion: your earlier calc included system tokens and embeddings refresh tasks. For the dedicated inference workload we care about 1-2B user tokens/month primarily from real-time inference. The 44M above is only the web app layer; we have background batch jobs (indexing/embeddings) that add ~1B tokens/month. Combined we land in the 1.1–1.4B range.

Procurement: looping in procurement; procurement@acmeai.com is on copy.

Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmeai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rachel Li <rachel.li@acmeai.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - follow-up pricing model

Jordan — thanks for the breakdown and context. I've updated our model with the split you provided (real-time inference + background jobs). Key assumptions below and a summarized per-1M token estimate.

Assumptions (please confirm):
- Effective tokens/month (combined): 1.2B – 1.4B
- Model: 8k context Llama-2-like (8k attention window), quantized to 4-bit in production.
- Throughput target: sustain p95 < 300ms at expected concurrency; peak tolerance for spikes up to 300 concurrent.
- Preferred GPU: H100 if available (better perf/$ at scale), fallback A100 80GB.

Redwood preliminary unit economics (all-in cost to AcmeAI):
- Engineering note: token -> GPU-hour conversion assumed: avg 12 tokens per GPU-second on H100 (8k context, batched), ~8 tokens/sec on A100 (conservative).
- Infrastructure & ops markup applied to cover reserved capacity pricing, monitoring, SLA.

Estimated cost to customer per 1M tokens (rounded):
- 4x A100 reserved pool: $1,450 / 1M tokens
- 8x A100 reserved pool: $1,000 / 1M tokens
- 8x H100 reserved pool: $780 / 1M tokens

Sizing recommendation:
- Starter: 4x A100 (for pilot, cost higher but lower commitment). Handles baseline ~150 concurrent.
- Production: 8x H100 (recommended if region supports) — meets throughput and brings unit cost to target range.
- Burst: optional shared burst pool (on-demand) to absorb spikes; pricing billed on usage.

I've attached the updated calc (Dedicated_pricing_calc.xlsx) with token->GPU-hour math and cost line items. Ben/Aditya — flag anything I missed.

If this looks reasonable we can 1) mark a preferred GPU and sizing, 2) produce a 12-month reserved quote + PO terms, and 3) schedule a technical deep-dive (Aditya) on perf testing.

Best,
Marissa

- Attach a usage band: if >1.6B tokens/month, trigger tiered discount and revisit sizing.

Operational note: ensure SOW calls out perf testing window and rollback to A100 in region constraints.

I can approve the discount up to 15%; confirm and I’ll update the quote.

Ben
